#5258. «Они сделают все, чего мы не хотели». Коалиция Вучича проиграла выборы в Сербии. Как это отразится на отношениях с Россией?

Бывший президент Сербии Александр Вучич заявил, что возглавляемая им коалиция «Объединенная Сербия» проиграла досрочные парламентские выборы.

Политик обвинил американское «глубинное государство» и силы из ряда европейских стран в содействии поражению его коалиции. Во время пресс-конференции в штаб-квартире своего движения Вучич заявил, что итоги голосования стали подтверждением «революции», которая проходила при непосредственной поддержке некоторых европейских государств и противников действующей американской администрации.

После поражения коалиции «Объединенная Сербия» на досрочных парламентских выборах страна может ввести санкции против России, считает Вучич. По его словам, подобное решение могут принять уже к весне следующего года.

Меня беспокоит, что не пройдет время до марта-апреля, как у нас будут санкции против России, они сделают все, чего мы не хотели

Как подчеркнул бывший сербский лидер, он не собирается препятствовать политическим конкурентам.

Досрочные парламентские выборы в Народную Скупщину прошли 25 октября. В голосовании участвовали 19 политических сил, претендующих на 250 депутатских мест в парламенте. Основными соперниками стали коалиция Вучича и гражданская группа «Студенческий список — студенты побеждают». Преодолеть трехпроцентный барьер еще может объединение вице-премьера и главы МВД Ивицы Дачича «Фактор стабильности».

После закрытия участков Республиканская избирательная комиссия сообщила о рекордной явке. Всего в списках числились 6,5 миллиона избирателей.

Сторонники избирательного списка «Студенческий список — студенты победили» празднуют первые результаты парламентских выборов в Белграде

Тем временем в Белграде начали праздновать победу оппозиции на досрочных парламентских выборах. После того, как Вучич признал поражение своей коалиции, представители протестного движения «Студенческий список» поднялись на сцену в штабе. Среди них был врач Илия Срданович, возглавлявший список на выборах. Участники акции скандировали «Победа!» и «Студенты победили!»

Сообщается, что вскоре у бизнес-центра, где расположен штаб движения, начались танцы под музыку духовых инструментов. К празднованию присоединялись жители Белграда. Несколько дней назад в городе прошли массовые беспорядки, к столице Сербии начали съезжаться колонны сторонников оппозиции.

Студенческие протесты в Сербии начались в ноябре 2024 года после обрушения бетонного навеса на железнодорожном вокзале в городе Нови-Сад, в результате которого погибли 16 человек.

Трагедия вызвала возмущение из-за предполагаемых нарушений при реконструкции вокзала, недостаточной прозрачности государственных проектов и подозрений в коррупции. Студенты стали требовать публикации документов о реконструкции, расследования ответственности за катастрофу и наказания виновных. Акции быстро распространились по университетам и городам страны, к ним присоединились преподаватели, представители оппозиции и другие граждане. Протестующие также обвиняли власти в давлении на участников демонстраций и требовали уважать право на мирные собрания.

В январе 2025 года на фоне протестов в отставку подал премьер-министр Сербии Милош Вучевич. По его словам, события 1 ноября 2024 года «бросили большую тень», а Сербия «как будто застряла в этой катастрофе». В сентябре 2026-го Александр Вучич объявил о своей отставке. Исполняющей обязанности президента стала председатель парламента Ана Брнабич — первая открытая представительница нетрадиционной сексуальной ориентации (международное общественное движение ЛГБТ признано экстремистским и запрещено в РФ) на посту спикера парламента Сербии.

#5262. UN agencies appeal for help to protect weakest nations from super El Niño

United Nations agencies are appealing for help to boost resilience among the world’s most vulnerable communities already being impacted by the strongest El Niño on record.

It is due to peak in December, but the human impact of its associated extreme temperatures, floods and droughts is set to last into 2027 and beyond.

A super version of the weather pattern is defined by sea surface temperatures more than two degrees Celsius above normal in the central Pacific.

"The current event could be unprecedented in strength, literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades," said Celeste Saulo, head of the UN's weather and climate agency.

"We are already witnessing extreme weather events and expect this to multiply and cascade as El Niño intensifies," the World Meteorological Organization chief told a press conference in Geneva, alongside the UN aid chief Tom Fletcher.

They issued a joint call for "urgent and coordinated anticipatory action" to protect the most vulnerable communities already living on the edge.

"We cannot stop El Niño, but we can prevent many of its worst human consequences," said Saulo.

Fletcher said the weather system was a "wrecking ball" that would bring havoc to Latin America, eastern and southern Africa, Asia, and the Pacific.

He said the long-term impact "will be felt for months and potentially years to come ... because it's this overlaying of crisis on crisis and crisis".

He cited widespread conflict and displacement, soaring fuel and fertiliser and food prices, and international aid cuts which are also weakening countries’ capacity to respond to the shock.

"The risk is you have tens of millions of people pushed into humanitarian need," he explained, warning that 50 million people could face increased hunger.

Fletcher said the next two weeks were "the critical window to act".Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya need supplies ahead of heavy rains.

Southern Africa needs seeds and livestock. Central America needs livelihood assistance, while Asia and the Pacific must prepare for droughts, floods and cyclones, he said.

However, Fletcher warned that the damage from El Niño would not be limited to countries on the frontline.

"It will create economic shocks for the global economy and drive further conflict, displacement, migration," he said. "I am sounding the alarm that the humanitarian system ... cannot alone cope with a threat on this scale."

He called on countries, development banks and international financial institutions to get money moving "before that damage is done".

Fletcher said he had released $50 million to help 11 countries on the frontline, including Chad, El Salvador, Ethiopia, Somalia, and South Sudan.

El Niño warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure, and rainfall patterns.

It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to twelve months.

#5263. En Afrique du Sud, une foule d'une cinquantaine de personnes a battu à mort un étranger

Un ressortissant étranger a été battu à mort par une foule d'une cinquantaine de personnes à Durban, en Afrique du Sud, selon la police.

D'après la police, cet homme non identifié, qui aurait entre la fin de la trentaine et le début de la quarantaine, a d'abord été abordé par deux hommes au bord de la route avant d'être agressé par un groupe plus important. Il a été déclaré mort sur les lieux.

La police a ouvert une enquête sur ce meurtre, dont le mobile reste à déterminer.

Ce meurtre fait suite à une vague de manifestations contre les immigrés en Afrique du Sud cette année, dont certaines ont dégénéré en violences. Au début du mois, des magasins et des voitures ont été incendiés à Durban, ainsi qu'à Soweto, près de Johannesburg.

Le porte-parole de la police provinciale, Robert Netshiunda, a déclaré à la BBC qu'il n'était pas possible de spéculer sur le mobile du meurtre commis à Durban et que de plus amples informations seraient communiquées dès qu'elles auraient été vérifiées.

Le gouvernement a exhorté les manifestants à agir pacifiquement, tout en reconnaissant la nécessité de réformes en matière d'immigration. Il affirme que des dizaines de milliers de ressortissants étrangers ont été expulsés ou rapatriés depuis le lancement de sa campagne de répression au début de l'année.

L'un des groupes à l'origine des manifestations, « March and March », avait initialement fixé au 30 juin la date limite à laquelle tous les migrants sans papiers devaient quitter l'Afrique du Sud.

Plusieurs manifestations ont eu lieu avant cette date butoir, et des agressions contre des ressortissants d'autres pays africains ont été signalées.

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

Ces incidents ont poussé plusieurs pays, dont le Zimbabwe, le Nigeria et le Ghana, à prendre des mesures pour rapatrier leurs ressortissants, par crainte de nouvelles violences.

Le Nigeria a accusé les autorités sud-africaines d'être responsables de la mort de deux de ses ressortissants ce mois-là.

Le Ghana a également confirmé le décès d'un de ses ressortissants, Bashiru Isak, père de trois enfants, abattu au Cap lors de manifestations visant les ressortissants étrangers.

Sa mort a déclenché une crise diplomatique avec l'Afrique du Sud, qui a affirmé que l'ampleur des violences avait été exagérée.

L'une des figures de proue du mouvement « March and March », Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, a nié être xénophobe.

« Nous ne pouvons pas vivre avec ces gens depuis tant d'années et, maintenant que nous disons que c'en est trop, que ça suffit, on nous accuse d'être xénophobes », a-t-elle déclaré à l'émission « Focus on Africa » de la BBC.

L'Afrique du Sud est confrontée à des attaques xénophobes depuis près de deux décennies. En 2008, plus de 60 personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines de milliers d'autres déplacées lors d'attaques généralisées contre des ressortissants étrangers.

Ces derniers troubles s'inscrivent dans un contexte de pauvreté généralisée, d'inégalités profondes et de chômage touchant environ un tiers de la population active.

Les migrants sont souvent accusés de prendre les emplois des locaux, de contribuer à la criminalité et de peser sur les services publics, bien que les chercheurs affirment que ces affirmations générales ne sont étayées par aucune preuve.

Malgré ses difficultés économiques, l'Afrique du Sud reste l'une des principales destinations du continent pour les migrants en quête d'emploi, de sécurité et de meilleures perspectives d'avenir.

Reportage complémentaire de Pumza Fihlani à Johannesburg

#5264. ABC removes more episodes by sacked reporter Mahmood Fazal

The ABC terminated Mahmood Fazal's employment in May. (ABC News)

An ABC review of sacked reporter Mahmood Fazal's use of anonymous interviewees has found three more episodes of concern from Four Corners and Background Briefing.

Two episodes have been withdrawn and another has had a short segment edited out.

A separate ABC Ombudsman review into two Four Corners episodes is still underway, but Fazal says he "won't stop" reporting on Australia's underworld.

The ABC has withdrawn a further two episodes by sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal and edited another due to concerns about anonymous interviewees.

Fazal's employment was terminated in May after an ABC investigation into his appearance on a podcast with a former underworld figure last year, ABC managing director Hugh Marks confirmed at a Senate estimates hearing in May.

Since then, two episodes he reported for Four Corners, titled Cocaine Nation and Meth Highway, have been removed by the ABC due to accuracy concerns. A Background Briefing audio program he reported, titled Remy was 12 when she became a drug dealer, was also removed later in July.

In a statement, the ABC said it had completed a review of anonymous interviewees in all stories reported by Fazal for the two programs, which identified concerns with three more programs.

"The review found that in each of these cases, ABC verification policies concerning the use of anonymous interviewees were not followed to a level that meets our editorial standards," the statement said.

"Therefore, in order to ensure complete confidence in published content, we have taken the decision to remove them."

Further concerns over the accuracy of reporting by sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal are raised on Media Watch, including that a hire car was used to mislead viewers in the profile of a purported cocaine dealer.

Two stories  — Four Corners episode Silent Orders and Background Briefing episode Meet the teens at the frontline of organised crime — have been removed from ABC platforms.

A short segment contributed by Fazal in the Four Corners episode The Postcode Wars, in which he says he visits a drug "trap house", has been edited out.

"Outside of this segment the episode meets our editorial standards and will remain available online with an editor's note," the statement said.

"The ABC is committed to journalism of the highest standard. Maintaining the trust of Australians depends on upholding those standards and we take any concerns about our journalism seriously."

Fazal posted a video to social media on Monday evening that appeared to be a response to the latest episode removals, saying it felt like the ABC was "trying everything in their power to stop me from ever working again".

"Even though all my work was approved across different teams and departments, cross-checked and met the standards before broadcast, they've decided there's now different standards that are retrospectively being applied to all of my stories," he said.

"They want to make me a scapegoat? Don't give a s***. I won't stop."

He has previously said he was hired by the ABC for his access to certain sources, but that proximity had then been used against him.

Fazal, a former member of the Mongols bikie club, is an award-winning journalist specialising in reporting on crime, violence, imprisonment and terrorism.

His reporting has appeared in VICE, The Guardian, Rolling Stone, The Sydney Morning Herald, The Monthly and The Saturday Paper.

Earlier this month, the ABC announced its head of investigations and current affairs, Jo Puccini, was leaving the public broadcaster after a 25-year career.

She had oversight of Four Corners and Background Briefing.

Other senior managers at the ABC at the time of Fazal's reporting have already left the broadcaster.

#5266. 'Alarm bells': How Australia ended up back where it started

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

The number of younger Australians who own their own homes has stagnated, sitting at around the same levels recorded during World War Two, as the cost of living and rents rise.

Fewer than 40 per cent of 25 to 34-year-olds were listed as homeowners in the 2021 Census, and that rate is expected to have fallen since, according to analysis from social welfare charity Anglicare Australia.

This is equivalent to the homeownership rate recorded in the 1940s, before the post-war boom took hold as multiple policies prioritised construction and housing for veterans.

At the same time, home prices and rents have risen, putting pressure on younger Australians to save for a mortgage while living away from home.

A recent report from property data company Cotality has shown that rents in some parts of Australia have soared by 80 per cent over the last five years, since COVID-era rent freezes were lifted.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Anglicare Australia said that support lines for younger people are dominated by stress over housing security and related bills.

"It's almost impossible to have a call from a younger person who doesn’t mention the stress of rents or bills," Anglicare Australia executive director Kasy Chambers told SBS News.

"They are studying, working and contributing. But they are earning less than the generations before them, being locked out of housing, and struggling to build the security that past generations took for granted."

Home ownership has steadily declined across age groups since the 1970s, but younger Australians have felt the sharpest declines, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Angela Jackson, an economist at the Productivity Commission, the Australian government's independent economic advisory body, said home ownership is particularly hard for lower socioeconomic groups.

"It is a lot more expensive relative to people's incomes to get into the housing market than it was for Gen Z's parents or grandparents," she told SBS News.

"Which does raise alarm bells about broader equity."

Home ownership rates have declined generation on generation in Australia, off the back of the housing boom in the post-war era.

Liz Allen, a demographer and social researcher from ANU, described 1940s Australians as going through "tough times".

"There were issues with inequalities, especially around education, geographic and income and wealth inequality," she said.

"I think it would be fair to say that the inequalities faced in that period and the global shocks during that period surpassed those that we're experiencing now."

Home ownership across all ages was lower than it is today, with younger people aged 25-34 the least likely to own property.

Allen said that the years after World War Two saw the "rhetoric of a fair go", where government made a non-partisan effort to "rebuild Australia".

It was a time of rapid residential construction and increases in home ownership.

"There were policies on multiple fronts to get people to Australia, to get people in Australia in work, in paid work, and to get people established in life with good wellbeing, access to education, homes, and so on," she said.

Allen said that decades of governments have shifted towards short-term policy wins, and "kicked the can" of long-term housing "down the road".

"We're no longer in that mentality of building, but maintaining," she said.

"And that undermines the very notion that we are a growing population, that we have new forms of inequalities emerging, and policy has not kept with societal and economic change."

For many Australians, a home and the equity it generates over time will be their largest source of wealth and a source of security for children who may subsequently inherit it.

But for younger generations who take longer to save and pay off a home, the economic benefits can be diminished.

Jackson explained that the nature of work also makes it harder for Gen Zs to earn like their parents and grandparents.

"Work is more casual and can be more gig work, or less secure, which can make entering into mortgages and those long-term financial arrangements more difficult," she said.

"And then incomes themselves have changed over time. For lower entry-level jobs compared to more experienced jobs, the relative wage is also lower."

Anglicare Australia would like to see policy settings shift to support younger Australians aspiring to home ownership.

"The government has taken an important step by reforming property tax breaks that have favoured accumulated wealth over work. Now we need to build on that progress," Chambers said.

"One of the clearest places to start is Youth Allowance.

"We have a social security system that literally says a young person needs less money to live on simply because of their age. Our findings show they can’t afford rent on Youth Allowance anywhere in the country."

The government recently announced a $20.90 increase to the maximum Youth Allowance payment due to indexation, which will reach $1,087.20 in September. However the rate can be much lower depending on your age, living situation and dependents.

Meanwhile, the median weekly unit rent in Australia is just under $700, putting rentals out of reach for Youth Allowance recipients.

"Rent isn’t cheaper when you’re 23. Groceries aren’t cheaper. Electricity isn’t cheaper. Yet young people are expected to survive on the lowest payment in the system," Chambers added.

The group would also like to see a wealth tax, which could tax assets and reduce the pressure on income-reliant Australians who don’t yet own a home.

#5268. Назван способ уменьшить нагрев смартфона во время игры

Для того чтобы уменьшить нагрев смартфона во время игры, пользователям предложили использовать питание от зарядного устройства в обход аккумулятора. Об этом сообщает немецкое издание PC-Welt.

Проверенный способ назвал автор медиа Флориан Кастнер. При обычном подключении к розетке энергия расходуется одновременно на работу телефона и пополнение заряда батареи. Специальный режим позволяет приостановить зарядку аккумулятора и направить питание непосредственно на работу устройства.

По словам Кастнера, это уменьшает дополнительное выделение тепла, связанное с зарядкой батареи. Функция особенно полезна при длительных игровых сессиях, когда аппарат уже нагревается под нагрузкой. При этом она не устраняет нагрев процессора и других компонентов и не гарантирует полного отсутствия перегрева.

Специалист также посоветовал проверить фоновые приложения. Редко используемые программы можно ограничить в настройках батареи, чтобы они реже синхронизировали данные. При этом важные мессенджеры, почту и календарь не стоит полностью лишать фоновой активности — иначе уведомления могут приходить с задержкой.

В середине октября журналисты издания GamesBeat рассказали, что Grand Theft Auto VI может выйти на персональных компьютерах гораздо раньше, чем ожидали — в первом квартале 2027 года. Релиз игры на консолях запланирован на 19 ноября.

#5269. Wie der Vater so der Sohn: Ein schlechter Verlierer in Brasilien [premium]

Flavio Bolsonaro ruft wegen Verlängerung der Öffnungszeiten nach einer Annullierung der Wahl in der größten Demokratie Lateinamerikas und spinnt an einer Verschwörungstheorie. Präsident Lula schafft ein doch überraschendes Comeback – und muss die Aussöhnung in einem polarisierten Land suchen.

Nach dem ersten Durchgang der Präsidentenwahlen in Brasilien hatte Flavio Bolsonaro wie der sichere Sieger ausgesehen – und Präsident Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva schien geschlagen und abgehängt. Im zweiten Durchgang schaffte Lula das unwahrscheinliche Comeback, indem sich der bald 81-jährige Veteran neu erfand, die sozialen Medien entdeckte und die Bolsonaro-Gegner in so großen Scharen mobilisierte, dass das Oberste Gericht den Wahlgang um zwei Stunden verlängerte. So errang er am Ende sogar noch eine komfortable Mehrheit.

Sollte der Sohn des Ex-Präsidenten Jair Bolsonaro das Land regieren, der vor vier Jahren nach seiner Abwahl einen Putsch inszeniert und seine Anhänger – wie sein Vorbild Donald Trump – zum Sturm auf das Parlament in Brasilia aufgehetzt hatte und der von der Justiz zu einer 27-jährigen Haftstrafe verdonnert worden war, als er aus dem US-Exil in Florida zurückgekehrt war?

Eine Mehrheit wählte lieber den Fortbestand der alten Ordnung – „ordem e progresso“, „Ordnung und Fortschritt“, wie es im Staatsmotto heißt. Wie zum Beweis ruft Bolsonaro Jr. – nicht nur äußerlich ein Abziehbild seines Vaters, weniger charismatisch und auch weniger radikal – nach einer Annullierung der Wahl. Dabei hat auch seine Partei in einigen Landesteilen eine Verlängerung der Öffnungszeiten urgiert. Mit den demokratischen Spielregeln halten es die Bolsonaros nicht. Wie der Vater so der Sohn: Flavio Bolsonaro zeigt sich als schlechter Verlierer und spinnt nun an einer Verschwörungstheorie. So schnell will er sich nicht geschlagen geben.

Brasilien ist gespalten, und Lula muss nun mit einem von den Konservativen dominierten Kongress einen Ausgleich finden. Der alte Mann der brasilianischen Politik, seit mehr als vier Jahrzehnten ein Fixpunkt, hat die Zeichen der Zeit erkannt. Die Bolsonaro-Bewegung bleibt trotz der Wahlniederlage freilich ein bestimmender Faktor.

Eines hat die Wahl im größten Land des Subkontinents indessen auch gezeigt: Der Siegeszug rechtspopulistischer „Trumpisten“ à la Javier Milei in Lateinamerika von El Salvador bis Argentinien, gefördert und gesponsert durch die „Amigos“ in Washington, ist einstweilen gestoppt.

#5273. Le Burkina Faso est « un petit pays », « pauvre » et « enclavé » : ces expressions que vous ne trouverez plus dans les manuels scolaires burkinabè.

Depuis la rentrée scolaire le 1er octobre 2026, les autorités burkinabè ont amorcé un processus de « décolonisation » de l'histoire enseignée dans son système éducatif.

Au Burkina Faso, la lutte contre l'impérialisme prônée par les autorités depuis la proclamation, en avril 2025, de la Révolution progressiste populaire, par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, passe aussi par une révolution mémorielle, foi des autorités.

Dans une déclaration le 7 septembre 2026, le ministre de l'Enseignement secondaire et de la formation professionnelle et technique, Pr Moumouni Zoungrana a indiqué qu'il y avait dans les cours d'histoire et de géographie « des expressions qui ne nous honorent pas ».

« Ce qui veut dire que dans nos manuels aussi, il y a des contrevérités qui sont consignées pour nous infantiliser, pour nous diminuer, pour nous abêtir. Et nous avons passé notre temps à faire la promotion de ces antivaleurs que nous avons transmises de génération en génération », avait-il commenté avant d'inviter le monde éducatif burkinabè à avoir « le courage de casser totalement la table et de la reverser ».

Le professeur Zoungrana a alors annoncé une révision des curricula notamment les cours d'Histoire, de Géographie et d'Education civique, afin dit-il, d'extirper les expressions « incohérentes ».

Ces trois matières sont considérées comme les plus urgentes alors que le pays préparait une refondation générale de l'école burkinabè baptisée « Pacte Neekre » (réveil en français) lancé le 17 octobre dernier.

En attendant la réécriture complète de ces manuels d'histoire, géographie et d'éducation civique, une note contenant quelques changements immédiats a été disséminée aux enseignants.

Ces changements vont du remplacement de certaines expressions, à l'introduction de nouveaux chapitres en passant par le bannissement de certaines expressions et chapitres

Voici quelques expressions et cours qui ont changé au Burkina Faso depuis le 1er octobre dernier :

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

En Histoire vingt-sept mots et expressions disparaissent du vocabulaire des enseignants et élèves.

Les envahisseurs et les espions : Parmi les concepts remplacés, la colonisation devient l'invasion impérialiste, le colon ou le colonisateur est appelé envahisseur et les explorateurs deviennent des espions puis les colonies, territoires envahis.

L'invasion impérialiste française du Burkina Faso est désormais l'expression utilisée pour qualifier la Colonisation française du Burkina Faso de

La libération de l'Afrique : La décolonisation et les indépendances sont désormais rappelée Libération de l'Afrique. De même, on distingue deux époques : pré-invasion et post-invasion pour designer respectivement les ères précoloniale et postcoloniale.

La guerre de ré-invasion : Désormais le terrorisme des qualifié de guerre de ré-invasion. L'appellation tirailleurs sénégalais fait place à combattants africains de la guerre et anciens combattants devient vétérans africains de la guerre.

Des leçons en histoire comme la traite orientale et la traite négrière changent d'appellation pour devenir les déportations orientale et transatlantique des Africains.

En géographie, une dizaine de concepts jugés « déshonorants » disparaissent également.

Le Burkina Faso présenté comme pays enclavé est désigné par l'appellation pays continental, le terme ethnies est remplacé par Groupe socioculturel tandis que les faiblesses et limites du pays sont désormais présentées comme des défis et opportunités.

La notion de développement est tropicalisée et devient notion de développement endogène.

Le cours d'Education civique et morale (ECM) lui change carrément d'appellation devenant Education à la Citoyenneté et au Patriotisme (ECP).

Plusieurs expressions particulièrement descriptives et notamment en Géographie, sont désormais bannies du lexique scolaire. Les qualificatifs pays pauvre, pays endetté, petit pays, climat défavorable, etc. sont interdits.

Il est également interdit de quantifier les groupes socioculturels en pourcentage des ethnies ou en pourcentage des religions.

Certaines leçons dispensées en géographie notamment en classe de 4e disparaissent. On note la suppression de la leçon sur "le commerce triangulaire".

Le chapitre également consacré à l'étude « de la géographie physique de l'Europe a été purement et simplement supprimé », confie un enseignant joint par BBC Afrique.

« L'accent est plutôt mis sur les conditions naturelles et développement de l'Afrique », explique-t-il.

Dans le même temps, de nouvelles leçons d'Histoire et Géographie sont introduites aussi bien au post-primaire qu'au secondaire.

En 6e, une nouvelle leçon intitulée la notion de révolution voit le jour. Un thème sur lequel les autorités mise pour impulser un changement majeur. S'adressant à des jeunes burkinabè à l'occasion de la Journée internationale de la jeunesse en août dernier, le ministre Moumouni Zoungrana a déclaré que « la révolution a été la seule option possible pour créer une rupture, (…) pour assurer la souveraineté totale, économique, financière mais aussi politique » du Burkina Faso.

Deux nouvelles leçons font leur apparition dans les cours d'histoire de la classe de 5e. Il s'agit des titres les savoirs et les savoir- faire africains et les révolutions burkinabè. Ce dernier revient sur les idéaux de la Révolution démocratique et populaire ( RDP) du Capitaine Thomas Sankara qui a dirigé le pays entre 1983 et 1987 et la révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré en cours depuis fin 2022.

Chez leurs ainés de la classe de 4e on note l'introduction d'une nouvelle leçon intitulée la révolution haïtienne. Elle revient sur les mouvements de lutte pour la libération des peuples haïtiens, leurs succès et leurs erreurs. Dans son dernier entretien avec la presse, diffusé fin septembre le président burkinabè Ibrahim Traoré appelait d'ailleurs ses compatriotes à « lire l'histoire de Haïti et comprendre qu'il ne faut pas s'amuser avec ces gens-là », faisant références aux anciennes puissances colonisatrices.

#5274. Six times our politicians reminded us not to take politics too seriously

Scott Morrison runs into a child during a soccer match at the Devonport Strikers Soccer Club in Tasmania. (ABC News: Matt Roberts)

Politics is a serious business, conducted by serious people, for serious outcomes (usually). With so much at stake, this is as it should be.

So too, interrogating and analysing political developments each week is a serious business.

However, the strength of Australia's democracy isn't only a product of our system of compulsory voting and an independent electoral commission. Something far less tangible has also helped keep things on an even keel — our collective commitment to not taking things too seriously.

Over the past 25 years, Insiders has covered the many shifts in Australian politics, whether subtle or seismic, and we've never forgotten just how important this is. But we've also never forgotten how important it is to have a laugh at the absurd and ridiculous moments that have often become the most memorable.

Fortunately, we have the perfect people on the couch with us each week to help us see both the serious and the lighter side of politics. Those who know and observe up close the politicians themselves.

So, as Insiders marks 25 years on air, here are the top six times we were reminded the art of politics is sometimes more finger painting than masterpiece.

"Crash or crash through" is a tried-and-trusted strategy for many politicians.

It's less electorally effective when the target is a seven-year-old child.

For then-PM Scott Morrison, a 2022 election campaign stop in Tasmania quickly went from picture opportunity to meme-nightmare as some unfortunate footwork saw him fall and land squarely on young local lad Luca Fauvette.

It was another addition to the long list of examples reinforcing why many politicians should avoid trying to prove sporting prowess.

Fortunately, the only thing bruised were egos and everyone played on unharmed.

Be it political U-turn or classic policy pivot, there is perhaps no greater gear change than that from Father of the House Bob Katter in 2017.

In the wake of the same-sex marriage plebiscite, the northern Queensland MP was all smiles recounting the blooming of a thousand blossoms.

What no-one was ready for, but millions around the world would come to appreciate, was the whiplash from those smiles turning to the flesh-tearing terror of death-by-crocodile.

You don't last five decades in public office without knowing your audience and Katter has always managed to keep his constituents wanting more.

English is a complicated language full of rules; each riddled with exceptions. So, giving a speech can be a dangerous business.

For then-opposition leader Tony Abbott, an address to party faithful in the election year of 2013 delivered one of the greatest malapropisms of any Australian politician.

There are many places for wisdom, but it's unlikely Abbott intended for this to be one of them, much to the delight of an army of pun-drunk sub-editors around the world.

Still, the slip of the tongue did little damage, he would be prime minister within weeks.

Of the many characters thrown up by the Australian political system, there have been none quite like Liberal MP Christopher Pyne, and even fewer who managed to earn themselves a single-word, slightly gangster-esque, instantly recognisable sobriquet.

During an afternoon TV interview in 2015, Pyne was being challenged to explain a $150 million funding issue in his government's higher education package.

Rather than provide answers, a clearly chuffed Pyne, instead flipped the switch to Vaudeville, saying he wanted the answer to be a surprise.

He did, however, promise the funding issue had been resolved. While not quite an origin story worthy of a Batman villain, "The Fixer" was born.

Most politicians love a stage, especially one that allows them to bask in the limelight of a full house.

At a charity event in 2011, Kevin Rudd, already both prime minister and former prime minister, as well as future prime minister and future, former prime minister (what a time we have had), took to the stage ready to rev up his base.

Rudd was in his element and was hardly going to let a croaky voice and an inability to sing stop him performing.

The result was hard to hear and impossible to forget.

Loyalty is a precious commodity in politics and especially rare in Canberra during the 2010s.

However, any leader should be so lucky as to have the blind faith of Bill Shorten.

So committed to his leader's position, he didn't even need to know what it was before dutifully agreeing with it entirely — no matter what it may be.

The result was a baffling, but nonetheless highly entertaining display of Labor Party solidarity.

#5276. 'Contaminated': How deadly bird flu crossed a new threshold in Australia

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

The "devastating" H5N1 variant of avian influenza marked a grim milestone on Sunday as the first confirmed case of transmission between bird and mammal species was recorded, with experts warning the worst is yet to come.

A long-nosed fur seal was confirmed to have died of the disease in coastal South Australia, with a second case being investigated in a seal in The Pages Conservation Park islands near Kangaroo Island on Monday.

Earlier, Environment Minister Murray Watt said the country needed to be "realistic" about the impact this illness will have on native wildlife.

"We are likely to see mass mortalities of birds and mammals, and I know that is a very distressing thing for Australians to hear," Watt told ABC television.

Sean Dooley of the avian conservation group BirdLife Australia told SBS News that the virus could have an ecology-shifting impact.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Potential extinction from the disease is possible for some birds," he said.

"That's why we need an effective response, where we can, to mitigate the losses.

"We also need a massive increase in the resources that go into ensuring resilient populations of as many of our species, or else we're going to be facing a real ongoing crisis beyond the actual outbreak."

Avian influenza, a flu-type virus, is airborne and contracted by birds and other mammals when they breathe or ingest it from an infected animal.

Robyn Alders, an honorary professor at the Development Policy Centre at Australian National University, told SBS News that the virus also survives outside of a host animal.

"Even if you can't see a diseased carcass or a dead animal, it doesn't mean that the environment there is safe," she said.

"Particularly now that we're starting to see areas where you've got larger die-offs, the potential contamination in that area is going to be significant."

In cooler temperatures where water is present, Alders said there is evidence H5N1 can survive for days.

In areas where the virus has yet to arrive, Dooley recommends people continue spending time in nature and report anything they suspect could be bird flu-related to the emergency animal disease hotline.

"That's still really valuable because it can help slow the spread as they remove those birds which are potential sources of infection," he said.

Cats are particularly susceptible to the disease, and Alders recommends people keep their cats indoors as the virus has a "50 per cent" mortality rate for them.

Bird flu vaccinations are underway in specific, suitable populations at the moment, but experts question whether the government is adequately prepared.

Dooley said the country is in a stronger position now than it was a few years ago, but that government claims to have "done everything they could" are false.

"If you talk to people on the ground ... it's really hit and miss as to whether people have been trained for this, or whether they have the equipment, whether the PPE they need is filtering down.

"There's a lot of people panicking because they don't know what to do and they're not resourced to do it."

Agriculture Minister Julie Collins has said the government is investigating whether bird flu vaccine trials for marine mammals in North America could be used in Australia — but that there is "nothing commercially available" which could protect vulnerable native seals.

While various avian influenza strains already exist in Australia, H5N1 is "so unlike any other bird flu virus we've dealt with", Alders said.

First detected in geese in China in 1996, the strain has flared up in the past but typically burnt out because it is simply too lethal.

The fact the current lineage exists at all is down to human activity, Alders argued, particularly the concentrated nature of poultry farming which creates huge viral reservoirs.

"A virus that kills its host within 48 hours — and that's what it does in chickens — shouldn't survive," she said.

"I don't know where this virus is going, but what I do know is that it was human activity that, in many ways, facilitated this virus to continue and to spread."

She said it's "up to us" to reduce and eliminate the virus.

"Everybody's got to be part of the discussion about how we produce our food, what standards we expect, not only in terms of human welfare but also animal welfare, and really working with agroecological cycles — not thinking that we can cut corners.

Red Bull Salzburg hat das Spitzenspiel der Fußball-Bundesliga gewonnen und ist nun als einziger Club Tabellenführer Rapid auf den Fersen. Die Roten Bullen gewannen am Sonntag zum Abschluss der zehnten Runde bei Meister LASK dank dreier Treffer von Torjäger Haris Tabaković (25., 49., 74.) mit 3:1 (1:1). Die Salzburger sind weiter ungeschlagen und liegen drei Punkte hinter Rapid, während der LASK als Tabellendritter schon acht Zähler Rückstand auf die Spitze hat.LASK-Trainer Dietmar Kühbauer ließ alle drei Torschützen vom Champions-League-Sieg bei Sporting Lissabon (Sasa Kalajdzic, Christoph Lang und Krystof Danek) zunächst auf der Ersatzbank und nahm vier Änderungen vor. Die Linzer übernahmen in der Anfangsphase das Kommando und stellten die Salzburger Defensive mit dem schnellen Sturm-Duo Moses Usor und Samuel Adeniran vor Probleme.Das brachte früh Erfolg. Bei einem Konter in Überzahl setzte Sascha Horvath Adeniran ein, der ins lange Eck abschloss (13.). Mit ihrer ersten Chance glichen die Salzburger aus, Tabaković verwertete einen idealen Pass von Jesper Lindström (25.). Die Mannschaft von Trainer Danny Röhl fand danach besser ins Spiel. Kurz nach dem Seitenwechsel bewies Tabaković einmal mehr seine Abschlussqualitäten. Der bosnische Routinier wurde von Sota Kitano perfekt freigespielt und donnerte den Ball ins Netz (49.). Die Salzburger waren nun das klar bessere Team und hatten durch Lindström die erste große Chance auf das dritte Tor, LASK-Torhüter Lukas Jungwirth konnte nach einem starken Solo des Dänen gerade noch mit dem Fuß abwehren (60.).

Kühbauer brachte danach Kalajdzic und Danek und später auch noch Lang, doch Tabaković dämpfte schnell die Hoffnungen auf einen Umschwung. Nachdem Kitano gescheitert war, stand der Stürmer goldrichtig, drückte den Abpraller über die Linie (74.) und schloss mit seinem siebenten Treffer zu LASK-Stürmer Lang an der Spitze der Torschützenliste auf. #5281. Egypt urges political solution to conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthis

Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty on Thursday said all options must be explored to find a political solution between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

Saudi Arabia, fighting in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government, has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh's airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years.

At a press conference where he reiterated solidarity with Saudi Arabia, Abdelatty stressed "the necessity of exploring all avenues for reaching political solutions that guarantee a complete withdrawal from the territories occupied recently".

The Houthis launched a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast, following the collapse in July of a years-long truce in Yemen's civil war.

The Houthis also declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude, and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities.

In response, the Saudi air force has frequently attacked areas under Houthi control, which include much of impoverished Yemen, where more than 250,000 people have been internally displaced by the fighting.

#5282. Le Nigeria confirme un cas d'Ebola lié à l'Afrique de l'Est

Le Nigeria a enregistré mardi un cas d'Ebola chez une patiente qui avait voyagé d'Ouganda, en Afrique de l'Est, à Abuja, la capitale de cet État d'Afrique de l'Ouest.

Le ministre de la Santé, Muhammad Ali Pate, a déclaré que le diagnostic avait été confirmé par des analyses de laboratoire.

Le patient est en isolement et reçoit des soins médicaux après son admission dans un hôpital d'Abuja.

Une source a indiqué à la BBC que le patient n'est pas nigérian, alors que les spéculations continuent à travers le pays concernant la nationalité du porteur et d'autres détails.

Les autorités sanitaires ont entamé un travail de recherche des contacts afin de prévenir toute propagation ultérieure, et 44 personnes ayant été en contact étroit avec la femme ont été identifiées.

Le Nigeria, premier État d'Afrique de l'Ouest à signaler un cas lié à la crise actuelle d'Ebola en Afrique de l'Est, avait réussi à stopper une précédente épidémie en 2014.

Par ailleurs, le ministère de la Santé ougandais a réagi après la confirmation par le Nigéria que le patient avait transité par son territoire au début du mois.

Dans un communiqué publié sur X, le ministère a indiqué que l'Ouganda ne comptait actuellement aucun cas actif d'Ebola, mais a reconnu que le patient avait transité par le pays.

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

Ils ont confirmé que la patiente s'était rendue dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo avant de revenir par l'Ouganda en direction du Nigéria.

Elle n'a présenté aucun symptôme d'Ebola pendant son séjour en Ouganda, ce qui, selon les autorités, a réduit le risque immédiat pour la population, mais l'enquête se poursuit.

Ebola est une maladie rare mais mortelle causée par un virus. À mesure que la maladie progresse, des vomissements et des diarrhées apparaissent et peuvent entraîner une défaillance multiviscérale. Certains patients, mais pas tous, développent des hémorragies internes et externes.

La maladie se transmet d'une personne à l'autre par contact avec des fluides corporels infectés tels que le sang ou les vomissements.

L'épidémie en République démocratique du Congo, qui a débuté en mai, a fait au moins 4 600 morts et plus de 9 500 cas ont été recensés, selon le Centre européen de prévention et de contrôle des maladies.

Elle a été causée par l'espèce Ebola Bundibugyo, relativement rare, pour laquelle il n'existe aucun vaccin ni traitement approuvé – bien que des essais soient en cours.

Peu après l'annonce de l'épidémie, des cas ont également été signalés en Ouganda, où au moins deux personnes sont décédées. L'Ouganda s'est déclaré exempt de la maladie en août, après la sortie de son dernier patient.

La maladie s'est également propagée au Kenya, qui a signalé au moins neuf cas d'infection.

Lundi, les États-Unis ont conseillé à leurs citoyens de reconsidérer tout voyage au Kenya en raison des risques sanitaires et ont relevé leur niveau d'alerte aux voyageurs pour ce pays.

Depuis le début de l'épidémie, le Nigéria a renforcé la surveillance des maladies, le Centre nigérian de contrôle des maladies émettant des conseils de santé publique aux voyageurs.

L'agence indique que les voyageurs en provenance de pays où la transmission du virus Ebola est active ou pertinente pourraient être tenus de remplir une déclaration de santé. Les voyageurs arrivant d'autres pays en sont actuellement exemptés.

Elle a également exhorté les voyageurs à rester vigilants et à consulter rapidement un médecin s'ils développent des symptômes d'Ebola.

En 2014, le Nigéria est parvenu à maîtriser une épidémie d'Ebola qui a causé au moins huit décès.

#5283. Michael Jordan had his ‘Flu Game’. Now Australia’s UFC legend has his own version

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Michael Jordan was violently ill before game five of the 1997 NBA finals, but somehow played through severe discomfort to score 38 points and give the Chicago Bulls a 3-2 lead over the Utah Jazz, setting them up to win the series in their next game.

Nearly 30 years later, it’s still talked about. The ‘Flu Game’ was one of Jordan’s most memorable performances, and a core moment in his own sporting mythology – even though, as it turned out, he actually had food poisoning, not the flu.

Alexander Volkanovski has just produced his own version, one that might soon be looked back upon the same way.

Days out from his UFC featherweight title defence against previously undefeated Russian contender Movsar Evloev, Volkanovski was feeling rough. His breathing was heavy, to the point where he was genuinely worried he might not last five rounds. It was later revealed that he was suffering from a chest infection.

He was offered medication that was perfectly legal to take, but Volkanovski was worried it might somehow be perceived as giving him an unfair advantage.

And he liked the idea of making things harder for himself. So he refused.

“Not many people, I guess, would choose to do that,” he said on Monday, hinting that there was “more to the story” which he’ll tell another day.

“I looked at it as more of a challenge. I was like, ‘No, no, I like the idea of this being more of a challenge.’ I’m just weird like that. Put it this way: my team weren’t happy with me, but I guess they’re not surprised as well.

“Most people would probably panic and freak out. I’ll look at it like, ‘Hey, when this story is told, it’s just going to make that so much better.’ And that’s how it was.”

Indeed, what followed was, by his own assessment, the greatest moment of Volkanovski’s great career to date.

Volkanovski saw off Evloev with a second-round TKO finish at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, his record ninth featherweight title-fight win – and he got it done quickly, just as he’d promised his wife, Emma, as a belated anniversary present.

Hours later, he was back in Sydney, his belt proudly draped over his shoulder next to a shimmering diamond necklace, his face looking only slightly worse for wear, still coughing through the remnants of his illness.

“I think it has to be right up there. I really do think it’s right up there,” he said. “Undefeated fighter ... you know what? Yeah, I’ll probably say that tops it, to be quite honest.”

Volkanovski is obviously much closer to the end than the beginning; had he taken much damage against Evloev, he might have been talking about his retirement plans on Monday, rather than celebrating his latest victory.

Such is his exalted status now in the UFC world, Volkanovski is in the envious position of being able to effectively call the shots, and nominate his next challenge.

“I had a good chat with the bosses of UFC, Dana White and Hunter Campbell,” Volkanovski said.

“You’ve got those guys even saying publicly that, ‘What Alex wants, we’ll give him. We’re not really going to say no to Alex.’ They don’t usually say those types of things.”

Top of his list is Justin Gaethje, the reigning UFC lightweight champion.

Volkanovski has never held belts in two weight classes before; his only concern was that he would be seen to be “cutting the line” ahead of other lightweights. But Gaethje is 37, and the idea of both of them retiring afterwards and vacating their belts, so as to not hold up their respective divisions, appeals greatly to ‘Volk’.

And so does the idea of doing it in Sydney, if he can convince White and Campbell.

“Let these two old fellas go have a crack, and then we can just sail off in the sunset. I just feel like that’s something that’s never been done, a cool story, and I think that’ll be great for the UFC,” he said.

The word “story” came up a lot on Monday. Volkanovski is happy to let others worry about titles, numbers, statistics, legacies and the GOAT debate; he is only chasing new chapters that will transcend and resonate with people at a deeper level.

For all his achievements, Volkanovski acknowledges that mixed martial arts still occupies a different, slightly obscured place in the Australian consciousness to more traditional sports. His wildly popular cooking channel on YouTube and other long-form videos have helped him reach a broader audience, one that doesn’t necessarily care about what he does inside the octagon.

As long as people are connecting with him, whichever way they’re doing that, Volkanovski is content.

“This is a different sport, and I get that. I’ve tried my best to change it, and change people’s perceptions of the sport,” he said. “But it’s all good. I like that people know me outside of that as well. I’m not too fussed. Either way, they know who I am as a person.”

Whenever this story is finished, it deserves to be remembered as one of the greatest this country has seen in sport.

#5287. A common tax misconception could catch some Australians by surprise

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

It’s now easier than ever to sell your unwanted clothes or household items online in Australia. Many popular sites, from eBay, Depop, Facebook Marketplace to newly arrived competitors like Vinted, have either scrapped or limited their seller’s fees, depending on the location, value and number of items sold.

So when do you need to declare your online sales income to the Australian Taxation Office and pay tax on it?

The answer can be as messy as your wardrobe. Be aware there is no minimum value of sales that triggers taxation obligations in Australia.

Digging into the law reveals key questions to consider whether you’re spring cleaning your wardrobe to get some cash for the latest fashion, selling a more valuable asset, or starting to run a business.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Two of the biggest online sales sites, eBay and Amazon, are required to provide lots of transaction data to the tax office.

What about selling goods on other platforms? The tax office may be tracking that too. Its tentacles are vast, with more than 600 million transactions reported and matched to taxpayers every year from a wide variety of private and public sources.

Even if a platform is not required to report, the transactions may still be captured through credit and debit card payment systems, such as Stripe or Square.

The tax office can also request information from the banks. It may even gather information via insurers on unexplained wealth based on "lifestyle assets" – such as cars, boats or art – you may own. There are also examples of taxpayers being caught out with unexplained deposits leading to hefty tax bills.

Let’s say you found a dress in your wardrobe that you bought for A$250, wore once, but don’t like. So you decide to sell it on eBay or Amazon, rather than giving it away.

You list it and sell it for $100. While you’ve now got $100 more than before, you have really lost $150 overall.

This is not a sound business model. Anything you sell actually comes at a cost to you; think profit, not just sales.

The tax office is unlikely to be interested in these types of occasional, low-value, generally loss-making personal-type activities.

In this scenario, where you’re just cashing in on your existing wardrobe, the tax office is likely to consider it private in nature and just a "hobby".

This is unlikely to create a tax bill. However, you still may need to declare certain activity and have records to support your position.

What happens when you go from selling just a few old dresses to spotting a market opportunity? Perhaps you start to develop a pattern of buying vintage clothes from friends, family and op shops and selling them at a markup?

Now you’re putting in time and money with the aim of making a profit.

That sort of activity makes it more likely for the tax office to see it as a "business".

A business typically involves repeated and continuous activities. For example, regularly buying items to resell online for profit would be more likely to be considered a business.

Another factor to consider is how systematic you are being. Are you acting in a "business-like" manner? For example, the kind of records you keep, and whether you advertise beyond family and friends, will both be relevant.

While the value of sales can be a factor, be careful, as there is no clear dollar threshold for when activities will be considered a business.

But what data the tax office collects from eBay and Amazon provides a clue as to when you’re more likely to be asked questions. Amazon and eBay both share data for people who sell goods worth a total of A$12,000 or more in a particular year.

Earning more or less than that amount does not rule you in or out of running a business, and whether your activities are taxable or not. But if you are earning more than $12,000, you will be on the radar of the tax office – and more likely to be asked to explain your activities.

If you are running a business, you will need to declare income and can claim allowable expenses. You need to pay tax on the net business income.

Consider other tax obligations too. For instance, do you need an Australian Business Number (ABN)? Should you register for the goods and services tax (GST)? If you’re unsure, the federal government’s business website has useful resources.

Even if you only sell online occasionally, the tax office may be more interested if it involves higher valued goods — such as jewellery originally purchased for more than $500, or other personal items purchased for more than $10,000 – which you’re now trying to sell.

For these more valuable sales, any gain you make – if you managed to sell it for more than you originally paid – is taxable.

However, it gets a little murky if you have made a loss. In general, the tax office restricts how to use losses for these higher valued personal items.

If you’re still unsure whether your online selling is just a hobby, if you’re about to sell a valuable asset, or think you might have crossed over into running a business, don’t risk it — speak to a registered tax practitioner for advice.

Elizabeth Morton is a senior lecturer at Curtin Law School, Curtin University.

She has previously been contracted to co-facilitate a short-term training contract for tax and crypto facilitated by UNSW for the Australian Taxation Office and is currently a member of the ATO's Crypto Industry Working Group. This is unrelated to this article. Elizabeth has not received grant funding directly related to the content of this article. Elizabeth is a chartered accountant, fellow of the Tax Institute and member of the Institute of Public Accountants.

Lisa Greig is a lecturer in taxation law for accountants at the University of Melbourne.

She is affiliated with the Chartered Accountants Australia & New Zealand, The Tax Institute and the Institute of Public Accountants. She has previously been contracted to co-facilitate a short-term training contract for tax and crypto facilitated by UNSW for the Australian Taxation Office.

#5290. ABC investigations boss leaves as Four Corners probe continues

Jo Puccini is leaving the ABC after more than 25 years. (Supplied)

Award-winning ABC investigations boss Jo Puccini is leaving the public broadcaster after a 25-year career.

She had oversight of Four Corners and Background Briefing, which recently removed three programs by reporter Mahmood Fazal over accuracy concerns.

The ABC Ombudsman's investigation into Fazal's reporting continues.

The ABC's head of investigations and current affairs, Jo Puccini, is leaving the public broadcaster, the ABC has announced.

In an email to ABC staff, acting news director Donna Field said Puccini had shaped significant public interest journalism, leading to numerous Walkley awards.

"We wish Jo every success in whatever comes next," she said.

The announcement comes alongside a deepening investigation into the work of sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal. The long-running current affairs program falls under Puccini's oversight.

Puccini joined the ABC in 2000 from the Seven Network, working at Media Watch as a researcher, before moving to Four Corners, where she won three Walkley Awards.

She held senior roles at Media Watch, Lateline, 7.30, the National Reporting Team and ABC Investigations.

Puccini said it was time for a new chapter in her career.

"I'm proud of the journalism I've helped produce and the impact it's had on helping our audience understand the issues and events that affect them," she said.

"It's been an adventure and a privilege to work at the national broadcaster, an institution where I've made lifelong friends. It's now time for a new chapter in my career.

"I'll be watching and cheering you all on to great success and important journalism that will continue to benefit the Australian public."

Three stories by Mahmood Fazal have been withdrawn by the ABC. (ABC News)

Three stories by Fazal have been withdrawn by the public broadcaster in recent weeks over concerns about their accuracy.

Other senior managers at the broadcaster at the time of Fazal's reporting have already left the broadcaster for unrelated reasons, including Four Corners executive producer Mathew Carney, news director Justin Stevens and managing director David Anderson.

Once a member of the Mongols bikie club, Fazal switched careers, becoming an award-winning journalist specialising in crime, violence, imprisonment and terrorism.

He was terminated after an ABC investigation into his appearance on a podcast with a former underworld figure.

In recent weeks, the two Four Corners episodes Cocaine Nation and Meth Highway were removed by the ABC due to accuracy concerns, along with a Background Briefing episode titled "Remy was 12 when she became a drug dealer".

Further concerns over the accuracy of reporting by sacked Four Corners reporter Mahmood Fazal are raised on Media Watch, including that a hire car was used to mislead viewers in the profile of a purported cocaine dealer.

On Monday, Media Watch reported on claims that "Remy", who purported to be a cocaine dealer in the Background Briefing and a Four Corners episode, was self-styled Sydney rapper Charissa Habkouk, who said the core of her story was invented.

Ms Habkouk told Media Watch she considered Remy "an acting role and a favour to Mahmood".

"All of that … is a complete fable … there's no validity to [it] … [Fazal] knew I could play the part and look the part," she said.

Media Watch also alleged the Mercedes-Benz that "Remy" and Fazal drove around in the Four Corners episode was hired by the ABC and not owned by "Remy" as the program implied.

In a response to Media Watch, Fazal rejected Ms Habkouk's claims and said he stood by the "integrity of my reporting and the editorial processes that underpinned both programs".

"I reject the suggestion that I fabricated, staged or knowingly published information that I believed to be false," Fazal said in a statement.

The ABC has previously said Fazal's episodes were removed "following concerns identified about the veracity of sources used in the three programs".

"The ABC Ombudsman is already conducting an independent review of whether the Four Corners programs complied with the ABC's editorial standards," it said in a statement.

Puccini's departure comes on the same day the ABC has apologised for a Race Around the World episode containing remarks about mining magnate Gina Rinehart, despite the ABC Ombudsman finding it did not breach editorial standards.

The episode featured contestant Kate McGuinness describing a fictional scenario that involved a violent attack on Mrs Rinehart.

The ABC apologises for a Race Around the World episode containing remarks about mining magnate Gina Rinehart AO.

Managing director Hugh Marks said the segment fell short of community expectations.

"While the Ombudsman has found that the film did not breach the ABC's editorial policies, the ABC acknowledges the episode has fallen short of community expectations," Mr Marks said in a statement.

"The ABC apologises to Mrs Rinehart and to anyone else affected or upset by the publication of the film."

Mrs Rinehart's company, Hancock Prospecting, wrote to the ABC Board on July 23 calling on the ABC to immediately remove the material, publicly apologise and investigate how the material came to be published, with full accountability for those responsible, a company statement said.

McGuinness released a statement through the ABC last week, apologising to anyone she offended and saying the sense of humour featured in her films on Race Around the World was "farcical".

"In no way was it my intention to promote violence," she said.

"My writing is cartoonish and always satirical.

"Unfortunately, jokes do not land with everyone. Its purpose was never to be taken literally."

#5291. Michael Jordan had his ‘Flu Game’. Now Australia’s UFC legend has his own version

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Michael Jordan was violently ill before game five of the 1997 NBA finals, but somehow played through severe discomfort to score 38 points and give the Chicago Bulls a 3-2 lead over the Utah Jazz, setting them up to win the series in their next game.

Nearly 30 years later, it’s still talked about. The ‘Flu Game’ was one of Jordan’s most memorable performances, and a core moment in his own sporting mythology – even though, as it turned out, he actually had food poisoning, not the flu.

Alexander Volkanovski has just produced his own version, one that might soon be looked back upon the same way.

Days out from his UFC featherweight title defence against previously undefeated Russian contender Movsar Evloev, Volkanovski was feeling rough. His breathing was heavy, to the point where he was genuinely worried he might not last five rounds. It was later revealed that he was suffering from a chest infection.

He was offered medication that was perfectly legal to take, but Volkanovski was worried it might somehow be perceived as giving him an unfair advantage.

And he liked the idea of making things harder for himself. So he refused.

“Not many people, I guess, would choose to do that,” he said on Monday, hinting that there was “more to the story” which he’ll tell another day.

“I looked at it as more of a challenge. I was like, ‘No, no, I like the idea of this being more of a challenge.’ I’m just weird like that. Put it this way: my team weren’t happy with me, but I guess they’re not surprised as well.

“Most people would probably panic and freak out. I’ll look at it like, ‘Hey, when this story is told, it’s just going to make that so much better.’ And that’s how it was.”

Indeed, what followed was, by his own assessment, the greatest moment of Volkanovski’s great career to date.

Volkanovski saw off Evloev with a second-round TKO finish at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, his record ninth featherweight title-fight win – and he got it done quickly, just as he’d promised his wife, Emma, as a belated anniversary present.

Hours later, he was back in Sydney, his belt proudly draped over his shoulder next to a shimmering diamond necklace, his face looking only slightly worse for wear, still coughing through the remnants of his illness.

“I think it has to be right up there. I really do think it’s right up there,” he said. “Undefeated fighter ... you know what? Yeah, I’ll probably say that tops it, to be quite honest.”

Volkanovski is obviously much closer to the end than the beginning; had he taken much damage against Evloev, he might have been talking about his retirement plans on Monday, rather than celebrating his latest victory.

Such is his exalted status now in the UFC world, Volkanovski is in the envious position of being able to effectively call the shots, and nominate his next challenge.

“I had a good chat with the bosses of UFC, Dana White and Hunter Campbell,” Volkanovski said.

“You’ve got those guys even saying publicly that, ‘What Alex wants, we’ll give him. We’re not really going to say no to Alex.’ They don’t usually say those types of things.”

Top of his list is Justin Gaethje, the reigning UFC lightweight champion.

Volkanovski has never held belts in two weight classes before; his only concern was that he would be seen to be “cutting the line” ahead of other lightweights. But Gaethje is 37, and the idea of both of them retiring afterwards and vacating their belts, so as to not hold up their respective divisions, appeals greatly to ‘Volk’.

And so does the idea of doing it in Sydney, if he can convince White and Campbell.

“Let these two old fellas go have a crack, and then we can just sail off in the sunset. I just feel like that’s something that’s never been done, a cool story, and I think that’ll be great for the UFC,” he said.

The word “story” came up a lot on Monday. Volkanovski is happy to let others worry about titles, numbers, statistics, legacies and the GOAT debate; he is only chasing new chapters that will transcend and resonate with people at a deeper level.

For all his achievements, Volkanovski acknowledges that mixed martial arts still occupies a different, slightly obscured place in the Australian consciousness to more traditional sports. His wildly popular cooking channel on YouTube and other long-form videos have helped him reach a broader audience, one that doesn’t necessarily care about what he does inside the octagon.

As long as people are connecting with him, whichever way they’re doing that, Volkanovski is content.

“This is a different sport, and I get that. I’ve tried my best to change it, and change people’s perceptions of the sport,” he said. “But it’s all good. I like that people know me outside of that as well. I’m not too fussed. Either way, they know who I am as a person.”

Whenever this story is finished, it deserves to be remembered as one of the greatest this country has seen in sport.

#5292. L'île Maurice est secouée par les pires émeutes depuis des décennies après qu'une femme a été blessée par balle par la police

La police mauricienne a imposé un couvre-feu nocturne pour tenter de contenir les pires émeutes qu'ait connues l'île de l'océan Indien depuis des décennies.

Les manifestations contre les pénuries d'eau et le coût élevé de la vie, qui ont débuté il y a une semaine, ont dégénéré en violence vendredi lorsqu'une femme a été blessée par balle par la police à un barrage routier.

Les circonstances de la fusillade ne sont pas claires, mais le policier a depuis été arrêté et placé en détention provisoire.

Le Premier ministre Navin Ramgoolam a ordonné le couvre-feu mardi, mettant en garde contre ceux qui « agissent contre les intérêts du pays », qui est un centre névralgique du tourisme et des services financiers.

« Ceux qui ont perpétré ces actes devront en assumer les très lourdes conséquences, conséquences que méritent leurs actes antipatriotiques », a-t-il déclaré dans une allocution à la nation.

Le gouvernement a annoncé la prolongation du couvre-feu jusqu'à vendredi matin, conformément aux mesures convenues lors d'une réunion spéciale du cabinet mercredi.

Le rapport détaillait les pillages, la possession de substances explosives, les incendies criminels et les dommages causés aux commissariats, aux feux de circulation et aux caméras de surveillance lors des manifestations, et faisait état de sept policiers blessés.

Dans un communiqué distinct, le ministère de l'Éducation a annoncé l'annulation des cours jeudi et vendredi dans les établissements scolaires, prolongeant ainsi la suspension déjà en vigueur. Il a précisé suivre la situation de près et qu'une déclaration ultérieure concernant la réouverture des écoles serait publiée.

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

Au moins 94 personnes ont été arrêtées depuis le début des émeutes, et le gouvernement indique qu'elles pourraient être poursuivies en vertu des lois antiterroristes.

Parmi les personnes arrêtées, 16 sont mineures.

« Compte tenu du nombre de mineurs impliqués dans les émeutes », le gouvernement a déclaré qu'il envisagerait d'abaisser de 14 à 12 ans l'âge auquel les mineurs peuvent être détenus et poursuivis en justice.

Elle a indiqué que les agents de la police spécialisés dans la cybercriminalité surveillaient constamment les réseaux sociaux et enquêteraient sur les personnes publiant des discours haineux et incitant à la violence.

Des manifestants ont brûlé des pneus et bloqué des routes alors que les troubles s'intensifiaient au cours du week-end, des commissariats et d'autres infrastructures publiques étant vandalisés.

Ces troubles ont entraîné la fermeture des écoles et des transports publics, et les ambassades étrangères ont émis des alertes appelant leurs ressortissants à la prudence.

La police a signalé des incidents et des arrestations malgré le couvre-feu initial. Selon le dernier communiqué du gouvernement, la plupart des arrestations ont eu lieu mardi.

Lorsque les manifestations contre la pénurie d'eau ont commencé, le gouvernement a réagi de manière proactive en fournissant davantage d'eau aux ménages, selon Zoë McCathie, analyste chez Signal Risk, une société basée en Afrique du Sud.

Cette escalade a créé une situation plus « inhabituelle pour la sécurité du pays », le gouvernement ayant eu recours à la fermeture des écoles et à l'instauration d'un couvre-feu, a-t-elle déclaré à l'émission Newsday de la BBC.

« On n'a pas vu de manifestations de cette ampleur et de cette intensité depuis environ 1999. La réponse du gouvernement est donc logique et nécessaire », a-t-elle déclaré.

Bien que le gouvernement soit parvenu à « contenir le pire des troubles », il reste possible que des manifestations reprennent dans certaines régions, les pénuries d'eau devant persister jusqu'à la saison des pluies en décembre, a-t-elle déclaré.

#5293. Record-breaking trainer’s warning for punters on Melbourne Cup favourite

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Ciaron Maher says national pride is on the line in next Tuesday’s Melbourne Cup as he prepares a record number of runners to do battle against legendary Irish trainer Joseph O’Brien’s five starters in the big race.

Maher is on track to have eight runners in the Melbourne Cup, including the favourite Point of Law, who beat two O’Brien-trained horses Small Fry and Omni Man in the Geelong Cup.

He not only gained a golden ticket but denied the Irish trainer a chance to have a sixth runner in the great race.

Alongside Point of Law, Maher has Saint George, Juja Kibo, Middle Earth, Mr Monaco, Shockletz, Royal Supremacy and Zahrann sitting inside the top 24 in the order of entry while a ninth entrant Kings Valley is battling for a start.

The previous record was when Robert Hickmott saddled up six runners for owner Lloyd Williams in 2013.

O’Brien will race last year’s runner-up Goodie Two Shoes as well as Defiantly, Sons and Lovers, Trustyourinstinct and James J Braddock.

It means the master trainers from opposite sides of the world are likely to saddle up half the field and have the top six fancied runners in the race.

Maher agreed that national pride was on the line on Tuesday as local trainers battled the international raiders including O’Brien, who he described as “always a force to be reckoned with”.

“We don’t want [the Cup] going overseas. We want it staying here,” Maher said.

Australian trainers have won the past five Melbourne Cups after sharing six of the previous 11 Cups with overseas-based trainers. Apart from O’Brien’s quintet, there are four other horses with international trainers likely to gain a start in the race.

Maher won the race with Gold Trip in 2022 and finished third with Middle Earth last year behind Half Yours and O’Brien’s Goodie Two Shoes. O’Brien won the race in 2017 with Rekindling and 2020 with Twilight Payment.

Despite flying under the radar in the lead up, Maher rates Middle Earth among his best chances because he is a seasoned stayer who he believes is in better form now than he was this time last year.

But Point of Law has caught the attention of the O’Brien stable, their racing manager Kevin Blake saying they are “fearful of him”.

“He has clearly stepped forward since he’s been here and Ciaron will be hoping he steps forward again for the big one which he clearly has the potential to do,” Blake said.

Blake said he wasn’t prepared to declare just yet the best credentialled of O’Brien’s five runners with barriers and weather among the variables to be considered. He described the crop as “a solid bunch of stayers”.

Maher agreed Point of Law was one of his best chances and his ability was undeniable, but he sounded a word of warning for punters, reminding them the Cup will be just his sixth start.

“Whether he is seasoned enough will be the thing,” Maher said.

Maher declared Juja Kibo to be in career best form and King George’s run in the Cox Plate when he “rocketed home” had him excited.

Shockletz, who will carry just 51 kilograms in the Cup, reminds Maher of High Emocean which carried a light weight to run third in 2022, and he said Mr Monaco was a genuine two-miler.

The market has his other runners Zahrann and Royal Supremacy well down in betting.

O’Brien is due to arrive on Monday evening after attending the Breeders Cup meeting on the weekend.

Meantime, Melbourne Cup-winning jockey Jamie Melham will not ride on Derby Day after her attempt to overturn a suspension failed on appeal.

Racing NSW ruled on Monday that her four-meeting ban for careless riding aboard Marhoona would stand. However, she will return to the saddle at Flemington on Melbourne Cup Day.

Melham is yet to finalise a Cup ride but is expected to ride in the Cup, which she won aboard Half Yours last year.

Half Yours was withdrawn from this year’s race after suffering lacerations when he fell in the Caulfield Cup.
